O.outcome_detail: coverage and concentration of the 14 learning objectives

cells.quote: The FCI [1] is a 30-item multiple-choice assessment that probes students’ conceptual understanding of force and motion, contrasting Newtonian reasoning with common informal beliefs about mechanics. Physics instructors use it more widely than any other mechanics RBA [4]. The FMCE [2] covers content similar to the FCI, kinematics and Newton’s laws, in 47 multiple-choice items. Several items share a physical scenario and ask students to select the response consistent with their reasoning about that scenario. The FMCE includes a small number of items on energy. The EMCS [3] is a 25-item multiple-choice assessment focused on energy and momentum, covering concepts such as kinetic and potential energy, work, and conservation principles that the FCI and FMCE do not address. Together, these three assessments cover the core topics of introductory mechanics.
cells.note: The entry additionally reports that the three RBAs cover all 14 LOs with at least six items per LO; that exact coverage result is not stated in the supplied study text excerpt.

O.outcome_detail: Families valued being listened to by a warm, caring professional

cells.quote: "Noah's Ark (Australia) conducted semi-structured telephone interviews with 14 families participating in the RBI bootcamp training.
